answer: A newcomer can forge a thousand keys in seconds, so rewards should not pour out like an open river. Instead each identity's earnings drain through a narrow inlet: they vest linearly over 30 days, and any fraud proof filed during that window claws back the unvested balance. A Sybil farm must then keep hundreds of accounts doing real, checkable work for a month while its locked earnings stay exposed to slashing, so the attack costs more than the rewards it hopes to skim.
